data.narrative: The student selected API key authentication because the current service is an internal bootcamp application where simplicity and testability matter. They then reproduced an unauthenticated admin-access vulnerability, implemented an API-key boundary with constant-time comparison, and verified the public-versus-protected split with a complete 9-test authentication suite.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose API keys over JWT based on the service context and reduced implementation complexity.
dimension_scores.evidence: Selected API key authentication because the service needs a simple, easy-to-test mechanism without JWT token issuance and expiry complexity.

dimension_scores.observation: Reproduced the authentication failure, inspected the implementation, identified the missing authentication dependency, fixed it, and reran a dedicated regression suite.
dimension_scores.evidence: Unauthenticated GET /links returned HTTP 200 before the fix; module-04-verify-auth.py subsequently passed all 9 authentication boundary tests.

dimension_scores.observation: Recognized that administrative endpoints must not be publicly accessible and implemented a concrete authentication boundary.
dimension_scores.evidence: Added X-API-Key verification with hmac.compare_digest and protected the /links router while keeping /r/{code} public.

dimension_scores.observation: Applied fail-fast configuration, constant-time secret comparison, and explicit public/protected endpoint boundaries, while recognizing remaining abuse risks.
dimension_scores.evidence: Authentication verification covered missing credentials, invalid credentials, valid credentials, and preservation of the public redirect behavior.

dimension_scores.observation: Communicated the vulnerability, selected approach, implementation boundary, and verification evidence clearly.
dimension_scores.evidence: The Module 04 completion summary explicitly described the authentication boundary and the 9-test verification result.

strengths: Used reproducible evidence to diagnose and close an authentication boundary failure.
Made a context-aware API key versus JWT tradeoff instead of selecting an approach without justification.
Verified both protected administrative behavior and intentionally public redirect behavior.
data.recommendation: Next, strengthen the authentication design with key rotation, rate limiting, and explicit authorization/owner-scope checks so authentication is not the only abuse-control layer.

public_evidence.student_action: Implemented API-key authentication for the administrative link-management surface and preserved unauthenticated access for the public redirect.
public_evidence.technical_detail: Protected the /links router with verify_api_key using the X-API-Key header and constant-time comparison.
public_evidence.proof: module-04-verify-auth.py passed all 9 authentication boundary tests, including 401 for unauthenticated /links requests, successful authenticated requests, and 307 for the public redirect.
public_evidence.ability: Can implement and verify an authentication boundary around REST API routes.
public_evidence.reviewer_value: Demonstrates practical security engineering rather than only implementing a happy-path API.

concepts_demonstrated.evidence: Unauthenticated administrative requests returned 401 while valid API-key requests succeeded.
The /links endpoints require authentication while /r/{code} remains publicly accessible.
A dedicated 9-test authentication verification script passed after the fix.

teaching_approaches.detail: Used the concrete URL-shortener API to reason about public redirects versus administrative operations.

learning_style_signals: Responds best to incremental build steps and immediate evidence verification
